image_description: A close-up, high-resolution profile view of an African crocodile's head against a black background. The image highlights the textured, armored skin (scutes), the dorsal eye with vertical pupil, and the interlocking teeth along the jawline.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad and triangular with a V-shaped snout (narrower than alligator).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The snout tapers to a distinct point (V-shape) rather than the U-shape of an alligator, consistent with Crocodylus niloticus taxonomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Jaws are massive with numerous conical, interlocking teeth visible when mouth is closed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Teeth are clearly visible, conical, and appear to interlock correctly. The fourth lower tooth fits into the upper jaw notch as expected.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned dorsally on the head with vertical slit pupils and a nictitating membrane.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Eye is positioned on top of the skull. Vertical slit pupil is distinct. The texture around the eye suggests the presence of protective membranes/scales.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned at the tip of the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The extreme tip of the snout is cut off by the right edge of the frame; nostrils are not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is elongated and heavily armored.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only the head and neck are visible; the full body length cannot be verified.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is covered in thick, bony scutes (osteoderms) arranged in regular longitudinal rows along the dorsal surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible neck and cranial region show highly detailed, irregular but structured osteoderms/scutes with realistic roughness.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Scutes are dark brown to grey with a rough, heavily textured appearance.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Coloration matches (earthy browns/greys) and the micro-texture of the scales is extremely high fidelity.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Ventral surface is covered in smooth, rectangular scales that are pale yellow to white.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The underside of the jaw/neck is in shadow or out of frame; ventral scales are not clearly distinguishable.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are short and stout with webbed feet; forelimbs have five digits, hind limbs have four.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Limbs are completely outside the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and muscular, comprising half of total body length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Tail is not visible in this head-shot composition.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm species-level identification (Nile vs. other crocodilians) based on snout shape and scale pattern.
To analyze the micro-details of the scales for signs of AI 'smearing' or inconsistent specular highlights.
To ensure individual teeth are distinct entities and not fused with the gum line or jawbone, a common AI failure mode.

custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the transition between the hard scales and the softer tissue around the eye and mouth corners. AI often blurs these boundaries. Verify if the teeth look like separate objects inserted into the jaw or naturally growing from it.

metadata.class_label: African crocodile, Nile crocodile, Crocodylus niloticus
